# Qwen3.8-27B atdev W3 overlay

> **Part of [atdev-serve](https://github.com/atdev-company/atdev-serve): up to 14.2× faster Qwen3.8-27B inference on a single A100** (408.9 tok/s single-user decoding vs 28.9 for the original bf16 model on stock vLLM; 2.08× vs the best vLLM settings), while passing our accuracy gates (GSM8K within 1 point of the original model, long-context 36/36).
>
> **Code & install:** [github.com/atdev-company/atdev-serve](https://github.com/atdev-company/atdev-serve) · **Companion model:** [atdev-company/Qwen3.8-27B-atdev-DFlash2-d16](https://huggingface.co/atdev-company/Qwen3.8-27B-atdev-DFlash2-d16) (retrained tree drafter)
>
> **More models coming:** we are optimizing other widely used open models the same way. Follow [atdev-company](https://huggingface.co/atdev-company) for new releases.

A **3-bit weight overlay** for [`RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4).
It is **not a standalone model**: it replaces 400 linear layers of the INT4 checkpoint at load time
when served with [atdev-serve](https://github.com/atdev-company/atdev-serve) (vLLM 0.31.0 plugin,
`ATDEV_OPT=...,w3_mixed`). Embeddings, `lm_head`, norms, the MTP head and every layer not listed
below come from the INT4 base checkpoint unchanged.

Fewer weight bytes per decode step make single-stream (c=1) decoding faster on an A100: the overlay
is part of the atdev-serve c=1 "full stack" configuration (see the atdev-serve README for numbers).

## Files

| file | tensors | covered linears |
|---|---|---|
| `w3_gptqact_d30_mlpo.safetensors` (9.86 GB) | 256 layers | `mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj` of all 64 decoder layers, `linear_attn.out_proj` (48 GDN layers), `self_attn.o_proj` (16 attention layers) |
| `w3_gptqact_d30_qkv.safetensors` (2.68 GB) | 144 layers | `linear_attn.in_proj_qkv`, `linear_attn.in_proj_z` (48 GDN layers), `self_attn.{q,k,v}_proj` (16 attention layers) |

## Format

* 3-bit symmetric, group size 128, values `q` in [-4, 3], stored in the compressed-tensors int4 layout
  of the base checkpoint (nibbles `q + 8`, tensors `*.weight_packed` / scales), so the overlay drops
  into the RedHatAI INT4 module structure. atdev-serve repacks it at load time into a 3-bit planar
  layout for its W3 Marlin kernel.
* Quantized from the bf16 [`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) weights with
  GPTQ (static activation order, dampening 0.3), in the AWQ-smoothed space of the RedHatAI INT4
  checkpoint (`awq_smoothed=True` in the safetensors metadata), so the INT4 checkpoint's other
  parameters stay consistent.

## Usage

The overlay is loaded by [atdev-serve](https://github.com/atdev-company/atdev-serve). Stock vLLM cannot
use it, because the 3-bit layers need atdev-serve's W3 Marlin kernels.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/atdev-company/atdev-serve && cd atdev-serve
./install.sh && source atdev-env.sh       # or: docker compose --profile c1 up --build
./serve_c1.sh                             # downloads this repo by id on first start
```

`serve_c1.sh` sets `ATDEV_W3_SIDECAR=atdev-company/Qwen3.8-27B-atdev-W3-overlay`. `ATDEV_W3_SIDECAR`
also accepts `repo:file.safetensors` or local file paths (`W3_OVERLAY=<...> ./serve_c1.sh`).
`ATDEV_W3_LAYERS` selects the subset of overlay layers to use. The c=1 configuration uses all 400.

## Calibration data

* **Prompts**: only
  [`HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k)
  (`train_sft` split, MIT License) and [`openai/gsm8k`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/gsm8k)
  (`main`, `train` split, MIT License), decontaminated against the evaluation prompts, the GSM8K test
  split and MATH-500. Some prompts carry short system prompts / answer-language instructions written by
  the authors (agent-style system prompts, "answer in Korean").
* **Responses**: generated by the target itself (Qwen3.8-27B served as RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4,
  vLLM 0.31.0), greedy and sampled.
* **Samples**: 400 randomly drawn prompt + response pairs (ultrachat 200, ultrachat + Korean
  instruction 105, ultrachat + agent system prompt 46, GSM8K train 43, GSM8K train + Korean
  instruction 6), each truncated to 1024 tokens; 348,936 tokens in total. GPTQ uses 8192 activation
  rows per linear layer drawn from these tokens.
* The same prompt pool (same sources) was used to train the atdev DFlash2 d16 drafter.

## Results

Measured on the complete atdev-serve c=1 full stack as released (this overlay + the released
[d16 drafter](https://huggingface.co/atdev-company/Qwen3.8-27B-atdev-DFlash2-d16) + engine features),
1x A100 80GB, vLLM 0.31.0, greedy decoding, 96 fixed prompts.

| | best stock vLLM 0.31.0 (RedHatAI INT4) | atdev-serve c=1 full stack |
|---|---:|---:|
| decode tok/s per request, mean | 196.5 | **408.9** (**2.08x**) |
| GSM8K, first 300 test problems | 0.973 | 0.967 |
| GSM8K, full test (1319) | 0.9462 | 0.9500 |
| long-context retrieval (passkey / multi-key, 2k-6.5k tokens) | 36/36 | 36/36 |

In development, going from 4-bit to 3-bit weights on the MLP layers gave +6.5% c=1 decode speed, and
extending it to the remaining 208 linear layers gave a further +4.3% (same-session A/B runs, kernels as
shipped). The overlay changes the target model's weights, so outputs are not identical to the INT4
base model. The accuracy gates above are the acceptance criterion. Full tables are in the
[atdev-serve README](https://github.com/atdev-company/atdev-serve#results-at-a-glance).

## About ATDEV

This overlay was built by [ATDEV](https://www.atdev.co.kr). We optimize LLM inference for any model
on your target GPUs, with custom kernels, speculative decoding, quantization and serving-stack
tuning. Results vary by model and hardware; this release is one example, running Qwen3.8-27B **up to 14.2x faster** on a single A100. ATDEV also delivers end-to-end enterprise AI: an experienced team of forward-deployed engineers (FDEs),
full-lifecycle AI agent development, in-house RAG, document parsing and OCR solutions, and fine-tuning of
LLMs, VLMs, OCR and other deep learning models. For business inquiries, contact
[atdev@atdev.co.kr](mailto:atdev@atdev.co.kr).
